what_its_for: Tapinarof cream is used to treat plaque psoriasis (raised, scaly, red patches on the skin) in adults. It helps calm the inflammation in your skin that causes these patches to form.
how_to_take: Apply a thin layer of this cream to the affected areas of your skin once a day. Gently rub it in until it is absorbed. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream, unless you are treating your hands. Do not use this cream in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. You can apply it to skin folds and most body areas, but talk to your doctor if you have questions about specific areas.
dosing: Apply tapinarof 1% cream to the affected skin areas once daily. Only use the amount needed to cover the affected area with a thin layer. Do not use more than directed by your doctor.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store tapinarof cream at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, mouth, or inside your nose. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or wraps unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid using other skin products on the same area unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor about all other creams or ointments you are using on your skin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: folliculitis (tender, red, or pus-filled bumps around hair follicles) on treated skin, contact dermatitis (new redness, itching, or rash that seems worse), signs of a skin infection (increased redness, warmth, swelling, or oozing), any unusual skin reactions, or if your condition does not improve or gets worse after several weeks of use.
when_it_works: Many patients start to see improvement in their skin within 4 to 8 weeks of regular use. Some people may see results sooner, while others may take a little longer. Even if your skin clears up, continue using the cream as directed by your doctor. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Safety and effectiveness in children under 18 years of age have not been established. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before using this cream, as the effects during pregnancy are not fully known. If you are breastfeeding, consult your doctor, as it is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. No dose adjustment is needed for older adults based on age alone.
